# Database reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm db:docs` (packages/db/scripts/db-docs.ts). Do not edit: change the schema's comments in packages/db/src/schema/*.ts or the migrations, then run it again. -->

Every table of the Digital Bahi database with all its columns, keys, indexes, triggers and access rules, every enum and every database function. It is **generated** from a database migrated from scratch (so it is exactly what `pnpm db:deploy` creates) and from the comments written next to each table and column in `packages/db/src/schema/*.ts`; CI fails when it is out of date. Why the database is designed this way (ER diagrams, integrity rules, indexing strategy) is in [03-database-design.md](03-database-design.md).

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Tables | 97 |
| Columns | 1612 |
| Foreign keys | 257 |
| Unique constraints | 46 |
| Check constraints | 57 |
| Indexes (besides primary keys and unique constraints) | 124 |
| Triggers | 73 |
| Tables with row-level security | 91 |
| Enums | 39 |
| Functions | 14 |
| Migrations | 28 (last: `0027_push_tokens`) |

## How the database is set up

* **One PostgreSQL database, many businesses.** The database is `digitalbahi` (`digitalbahi_dev` on a developer's computer). Every business-owned table has a `business_id`; row-level security lets a connection see and write only the rows of the business it has set in `app.business_id` for its transaction. Tables without `business_id` are platform-wide (users, states, permissions) or are reached through their parent.
* **Two roles.** `digitalbahi_owner` owns the tables and runs the migrations. The API connects as `digitalbahi_app`, which does not own the tables, so row-level security always applies to it; it also lacks UPDATE / DELETE on the append-only tables (marked below), so history cannot be rewritten even if a trigger were dropped.
* **Conventions.** Column names are snake_case. Primary keys are UUIDs (append-only ledgers use bigint identities). Money is `numeric(15,2)`, rates `numeric(15,4)`, quantities `numeric(15,3)`, percentages `numeric(7,3)`; never floating point. Times are `timestamptz`; business dates are `date`. `created_by` / `updated_by` have no foreign key (users are never deleted). `version` is for optimistic locking.
* **Extensions:** `pg_trgm`.
* **Migrations** are in `packages/db/migrations` (SQL, applied in order by `pnpm db:deploy`); the Drizzle schema in `packages/db/src/schema` must match them (checked in CI).

**Reading a table below:** *Required* ✓ means `NOT NULL`. A foreign key is shown as → `table.column` (with its delete rule when it is not *no action*). Constraints over several columns, checks, indexes, triggers and row-level security follow each column list.

## Platform and tenancy

### `states`

GST state / UT codes. Reference data seeded from @digitalbahi/core GST_STATES.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `code` | char(2) | ✓ |  | **Primary key.** GST state code (01 Jammu and Kashmir ... 37 Andhra Pradesh, 38 Ladakh, 97 Other Territory); the first two digits of a GSTIN. |
| `name` | text | ✓ |  | Name as shown in the app and on documents. |
| `name_hi` | text | ✓ |  | Name in Hindi, shown when the app or a document is in Hindi (the English name otherwise). |
| `kind` | varchar(10) | ✓ |  | state, ut (Union territory) or special (codes such as 96 Foreign country and 97 Other Territory). |
| `state_tax_component` | varchar(5) | ✓ |  | SGST or UTGST for intra-state supplies. |
| `is_legacy` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | An old code no longer given to new registrations (25 Daman and Diu, 28 Andhra Pradesh before 2014), kept for old documents. |

* **The API's role may:** read (not insert or update or delete).

### `users`

A login identity. One user can belong to several businesses with different roles.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `name` | text | ✓ |  | Name as shown in the app and on documents. |
| `mobile` | varchar(15) | ✓ |  | Mobile number used to sign in and receive OTPs; unique across all users. |
| `email` | text |  |  | Email address (optional, unique when given). |
| `password_hash` | text |  |  | argon2id hash. Never selected by default in API queries. |
| `preferred_locale` | varchar(10) | ✓ | `'en'` | Language of the app and of messages to this person: en or hi. |
| `is_active` | boolean | ✓ | `true` | Inactive rows are kept for history but no longer offered for new entries. |
| `mfa_secret_enc` | text |  |  | Reserved for two-factor sign-in (not used yet). |
| `failed_login_count` | integer | ✓ | `0` | Wrong passwords in a row; at 5 the account is locked for 15 minutes. Reset by a successful sign-in. |
| `locked_until` | timestamptz |  |  | Sign-in is refused until this time after too many wrong passwords. |
| `last_login_at` | timestamptz |  |  | Last successful sign-in. |

### `businesses`

The tenant: one legal entity / GSTIN. Every business row in every other table carries business_id; the API scopes every query by it and Postgres row-level security enforces the same rule as defence in depth.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `legal_name` | text | ✓ |  | Legal name as registered for GST (printed on documents). |
| `trade_name` | text |  |  | Trade name, when the firm trades under another name. |
| `gstin` | varchar(15) |  |  | GSTIN (15 characters; format and check digit verified when entered). |
| `pan` | varchar(10) |  |  | PAN (10 characters). |
| `gst_registration` | [business_gst_registration](#enum-business_gst_registration) | ✓ | `'regular'` | Regular, composition or unregistered: decides whether it charges GST and can claim input credit. |
| `state_code` | char(2) | ✓ |  | → [`states`](#states).code. State of the principal place of business: decides intra- or inter-state supply. |
| `address_line1` | text |  |  | Address, first line. |
| `address_line2` | text |  |  | Address, second line. |
| `city` | text |  |  | City or town. |
| `pincode` | varchar(6) |  |  | PIN code (6 digits). |
| `phone` | varchar(15) |  |  | Phone number printed on documents. |
| `email` | text |  |  | Email printed on documents and used as the reply-to address for its emails. |
| `logo_file_id` | uuid |  |  | The firm's logo (in `files`), printed on its documents. |
| `financial_year_start_month` | smallint | ✓ | `4` | 1-12; 4 = April (Indian FY). |
| `time_zone` | text | ✓ | `'Asia/Kolkata'` | Time zone for the business's dates and schedules (IANA name). |
| `currency` | char(3) | ✓ | `'INR'` | Currency of its amounts (ISO 4217); INR. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |
| `version` | integer | ✓ | `1` | Optimistic locking: increases on every change; a stale write (or an offline edit made on an older copy) is detected by it. |
| `status` | varchar(12) | ✓ | `'trial'` | SaaS lifecycle: trial -> active; suspended/closed tenants cannot sign in. |
| `plan` | varchar(30) | ✓ | `'trial'` | Subscription plan of the SaaS (trial while on trial). |
| `trial_ends_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the trial ends. |

* Check `businesses_fy_month_chk`: `(financial_year_start_month >= 1 AND financial_year_start_month <= 12)`
* Check `businesses_status_chk`: `(status::text = ANY (ARRAY['trial'::character varying, 'active'::character varying, 'suspended'::character varying, 'closed'::character varying]::text[]))`
* Index `businesses_gstin_idx`: btree `(gstin)`
* Trigger `businesses_set_updated_at`: before update, each row → `set_updated_at()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation` (all commands), using `((id = (NULLIF(current_setting('app.business_id'::text, true), ''::text))::uuid) OR (id IN ( SELECT bm.business_id
   FROM business_members bm
  WHERE ((bm.user_id = (NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id'::text, true), ''::text))::uuid) AND bm.is_active))))`, check `(id = (NULLIF(current_setting('app.business_id'::text, true), ''::text))::uuid)`
* Referenced by: 88 tables by `business_id`

### `settings`

Configurable business rules as typed JSON values, one row per key, e.g. stock.negative_policy = "warn", invoice.round_off = {"mode":"nearest","step":1}, credit.policy = {...}, gst.b2cl_threshold = [{from, amount}], orders.workflow = {...}. Keys and value schemas are defined (and validated) in the API settings module.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `key`). → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `key` | text | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `business_id`). Setting name, e.g. stock.negative_policy or invoice.terms. |
| `value` | jsonb | ✓ |  | The setting's value as JSON, checked against the setting's schema in the API. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |

* Primary key `business_id, key`
* Trigger `settings_set_updated_at`: before update, each row → `set_updated_at()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `files`

Uploaded files (product images, receipts, logos, proof of delivery, backups). Small files such as the firm's logo keep their bytes in `content`, so they are part of the ordinary database backup; larger ones go to object storage under `storageKey`.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `storage_key` | text | ✓ |  | Where the bytes are: `db/<file id>` when they are kept in `content`, otherwise a key in object storage. |
| `original_name` | text | ✓ |  | File name as uploaded. |
| `mime_type` | text | ✓ |  | Content type, e.g. image/png or application/pdf. |
| `size_bytes` | bigint | ✓ |  | Size in bytes. |
| `sha256` | char(64) | ✓ |  | SHA-256 of the bytes (hex), to recognise the same file uploaded twice. |
| `purpose` | varchar(40) | ✓ |  | What the file belongs to, for cleanup and access checks (e.g. "expense", "product"). |
| `uploaded_by` | uuid |  |  | User who uploaded it. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `deleted_at` | timestamptz |  |  | Soft delete: when the row was removed from lists. Posted documents are never deleted. |
| `deleted_by` | uuid |  |  | Soft delete: the user who removed the row. |
| `content` | bytea |  |  | The bytes, for small files kept in the database (such as a logo). |

* Check `files_size_chk`: `(size_bytes > 0)`
* Index `files_storage_key_uq`: unique, btree `(storage_key)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* Referenced by: [`employees`](#employees).photo_file_id, [`product_images`](#product_images).file_id, [`dispatch_orders`](#dispatch_orders).pod_file_id, [`expenses`](#expenses).receipt_file_id, [`gst_exports`](#gst_exports).file_id, [`backups`](#backups).file_id

### `devices`

Registered devices (phones, desktops). Needed for offline work: each device gets a short series code so invoices numbered offline can never collide.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `user_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`users`](#users).id. The person using the device. |
| `name` | text | ✓ |  | Name shown in Settings -> Devices (browser and system, e.g. Chrome on Android). |
| `platform` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | web, android, ios, windows, mac or linux. |
| `series_code` | varchar(4) |  |  | The device's code for its offline bill series (A1, A2 ...): bills made offline are numbered A1/26-27/0001 and never collide. |
| `last_sync_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the device last sent work it did offline. |
| `last_seen_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the device last checked in. |
| `revoked_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the device was removed: it is signed out, its unsynced bills are refused and it deletes its copy. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `check_hash` | text |  |  | SHA-256 of the secret the device checks in with (renewed at each registration), so a removed device learns it must wipe itself. |
| `wiped_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When a removed device was told to delete its copy (it did so on hearing it). |
| `session_id` | uuid |  |  | The sign-in (refresh token family) the device last registered with: removing the device ends it. |
| `queue_waiting` | integer | ✓ | `0` | Work waiting on the device to be sent, as it last reported (bills, payments, orders, changes …). |
| `queue_bills` | integer | ✓ | `0` | Of that, bills. |
| `queue_refused` | integer | ✓ | `0` | Work the server refused that waits on the device for someone to fix or remove. |
| `queue_oldest_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the oldest waiting work was done. |
| `queue_reported_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the device last reported its waiting work (it can only while online). |

### `document_series`

Number series per document type and financial year. The next number is taken with UPDATE ... SET next_number = next_number + 1 RETURNING inside the posting transaction: numbers are gap-free and never duplicated.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `doc_type` | varchar(30) | ✓ |  | invoice, sales_order, purchase, payment_in, payment_out, credit_note, debit_note, expense, packing, dispatch... |
| `name` | text | ✓ |  | Name as shown in the app and on documents. |
| `pattern` | text | ✓ |  | e.g. "INV/{FYS}/{SEQ:5}" — see formatDocumentNumber in @digitalbahi/core. |
| `financial_year` | varchar(9) | ✓ |  | Financial year the series numbers, e.g. 2026-27; numbering starts again each year. |
| `next_number` | integer | ✓ | `1` | The number the next document will get. |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id. Set for per-device offline series. |
| `is_default` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | The series used for this document type unless another is chosen. |
| `is_active` | boolean | ✓ | `true` | Inactive rows are kept for history but no longer offered for new entries. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |

### `roles`

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |

| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |

   FROM business_members bm

### `refresh_tokens`

Rotating refresh tokens. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored. Re-use of a rotated token revokes the whole family (token theft detection).

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `user_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`users`](#users).id (on delete cascade). The person signed in. |
| `family_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | The sign-in (session) the token belongs to: every rotation keeps the family; reusing an old token revokes the whole family. |
| `token_hash` | varchar(64) | ✓ |  | **Unique.** SHA-256 of the token; the token itself is never stored. |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id. The registered device of the session, when it has one. |
| `ip` | varchar(45) |  |  | IP address the token was issued to. |
| `user_agent` | text |  |  | Browser or app that signed in. |
| `expires_at` | timestamptz | ✓ |  | When the token stops working (30 days by default). |
| `rotated_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When it was exchanged for a new token; using it again after that counts as theft. |
| `revoked_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When it was revoked (sign-out, theft detection, a removed device or member). |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `business_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id. Business the session is working in; kept per session so each device can be in a different business. |

* Index `refresh_tokens_active_idx`: btree `(user_id) WHERE (revoked_at IS NULL)`
* Index `refresh_tokens_family_idx`: btree `(family_id)`

### `otp_challenges`

One-time passwords for mobile login / password reset (hash only, short expiry, attempt-limited).

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `mobile` | varchar(15) | ✓ |  | Mobile number the code was sent to. |
| `purpose` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | What the code is for: signup, login or reset. |
| `code_hash` | varchar(64) | ✓ |  | SHA-256 of the code; the code itself is never stored. |
| `attempts` | smallint | ✓ | `0` | Wrong codes typed; the challenge stops working after the limit. |
| `expires_at` | timestamptz | ✓ |  | The code is valid for 5 minutes. |
| `consumed_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the code was used (a code works once). |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |

* Index `otp_challenges_mobile_idx`: btree `(mobile, created_at)`

## Stock

### `stock_ledger`

STOCK LEDGER — the single source of truth for stock. Append-only: the app role has no UPDATE/DELETE privilege and a trigger rejects both. Corrections are new rows (reversal or adjustment), so every unit is explainable: date \| transaction \| in \| out \| balance.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | ✓ | identity (always) | **Primary key.** Sequential row number (append-only table). |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `product_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`products`](#products).id. The product that moved. |
| `warehouse_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`warehouses`](#warehouses).id. The godown it moved in or out of. |
| `batch_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`batches`](#batches).id. The batch, for products kept by batch. |
| `txn_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date of the movement (the document's date). |
| `movement_type` | [stock_movement_type](#enum-stock_movement_type) | ✓ |  | What moved the stock: sale, purchase, return, adjustment, transfer, opening ... |
| `qty_in` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `0` | Quantities in the product's base unit. |
| `qty_out` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `0` | Quantity out, in the base unit (exactly one of qty_in / qty_out is above zero). |
| `balance_after` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ |  | Running balance for (product, warehouse, batch) after this row. |
| `unit_cost` | numeric(15,4) | ✓ | `0` | Cost per base unit: the landed cost for purchases, the moving-average cost at the time for sales and other issues. |
| `ref_type` | varchar(30) | ✓ |  | Source document: invoice, purchase, credit_note, adjustment, transfer, opening... |
| `ref_id` | uuid |  |  | Id of the source document. |
| `ref_line_id` | uuid |  |  | Id of the source document's line. |
| `ref_number` | varchar(40) |  |  | Number of the source document, for display (INV/26-27/00042). |
| `reason` | text |  |  | Why, for adjustments and corrections. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |

* Check `stock_ledger_direction_chk`: `(qty_in >= 0::numeric AND qty_out >= 0::numeric AND (qty_in > 0::numeric) <> (qty_out > 0::numeric))`
* Index `stock_ledger_date_idx`: btree `(business_id, txn_date)`
* Index `stock_ledger_product_idx`: btree `(business_id, product_id, warehouse_id, id)`
* Index `stock_ledger_ref_idx`: btree `(ref_type, ref_id)`
* Trigger `stock_ledger_append_only`: before delete or update, each row → `forbid_update_delete()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* **The API's role may:** read, insert (not update or delete).

### `stock_balances`

Current stock per product / warehouse / batch: a cache of the ledger updated in the same transaction (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the row, then insert the ledger row with the new balance). Reads are O(1); the nightly analytics job checks that it equals SUM(qty_in - qty_out) and reports any difference.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `product_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`products`](#products).id. The product. |
| `warehouse_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`warehouses`](#warehouses).id. The godown. |
| `batch_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`batches`](#batches).id. The batch (empty for products not kept by batch); one row per product, godown and batch. |
| `qty` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `0` | Quantity on hand in the base unit (can go below zero when the business allows selling before the purchase is entered). |
| `last_ledger_id` | bigint |  |  | The last stock_ledger row applied to this balance. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |

* Unique `stock_balances_uq`: `NULLS NOT DISTINCT (business_id, product_id, warehouse_id, batch_id)`
* Index `stock_balances_product_idx`: btree `(product_id)`

* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

## Purchases

### `purchases`

Purchase bill entry. Posting it (one DB transaction) increases stock, updates moving-average cost, credits the supplier ledger and writes inward GST rows.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `purchase_number` | varchar(30) |  |  | Internal reference number from our own series. |
| `series_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`document_series`](#document_series).id. Number series the purchase was numbered from. |
| `financial_year` | varchar(9) | ✓ |  | Financial year of the purchase (2026-27); its number is unique within it. |
| `supplier_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`suppliers`](#suppliers).id. The supplier who sent the bill. |
| `supplier_invoice_number` | varchar(30) | ✓ |  | The supplier's bill number; the same supplier's bill cannot be entered twice in a year. |
| `supplier_invoice_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date on the supplier's bill (decides the GST period of the input credit). |
| `received_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date the goods were received (the stock comes in on this date). |
| `due_date` | date |  |  | When the bill is to be paid (bill date + the supplier's credit days). |
| `warehouse_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`warehouses`](#warehouses).id. Godown the goods were received into. |
| `party_name` | text | ✓ |  | Party's name as printed on the document (snapshot). |
| `party_gstin` | varchar(15) |  |  | Party's GSTIN when the document was posted; empty for unregistered parties. |
| `party_state_code` | char(2) |  |  | Party's GST state code when the document was posted. |
| `billing_address` | jsonb |  |  | Billing address printed on the document (snapshot: line1, line2, city, pincode, state). |
| `shipping_address` | jsonb |  |  | Delivery address printed on the document, when different from billing (snapshot). |
| `place_of_supply` | char(2) | ✓ |  | GST state code of the place of supply (96 for exports): decides CGST + SGST or IGST. |
| `supply_type` | [supply_type](#enum-supply_type) | ✓ |  | Intra-state (CGST + SGST), inter-state (IGST) or export / SEZ. |
| `is_reverse_charge` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Reverse charge: the recipient pays this GST to the government instead of the supplier. |
| `tax_engine_version` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | Version of the calculation engine used (e.g. "gst-line@1"). |
| `itc_eligibility` | [itc_eligibility](#enum-itc_eligibility) | ✓ | `'eligible'` | Whether the GST on the bill can be claimed as input credit: eligible, ineligible (blocked), capital goods or input services. |
| `status` | [document_status](#enum-document_status) | ✓ | `'draft'` | Draft, posted or cancelled. |
| `gross_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Sum of the lines' gross amounts (qty x rate). |
| `discount_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | All discounts on the lines, including their shares of the document discount. |
| `document_discount_percent` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Discount on the whole document, in percent of the lines' net total. |
| `document_discount_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Discount on the whole document, in rupees (spread over the lines as `document_discount_share`). |
| `taxable_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total taxable value: the lines' plus taxed charges'. |
| `cgst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total central GST on lines and charges. |
| `sgst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total state / UT GST on lines and charges. |
| `igst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total integrated GST on lines and charges. |
| `cess_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total compensation cess. |
| `charges` | jsonb | ✓ | `'[]'` | Freight, packing etc.: [{key,label,taxable,gstRate,cgst,sgst,igst,cess,total}]. |
| `charges_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Freight, packing and other charges before their GST. |
| `round_off` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Amount added or taken off to round the grand total (to the rupee by default). |
| `grand_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | What the party pays: taxable value + charges + GST and cess + round-off. |
| `amount_paid` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Paid so far against this bill (payments allocated to it, and payment at the time of the bill). |
| `balance_due` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Still to be paid: grand total less amount paid and returns / credit notes against it. |
| `payment_status` | [payment_status](#enum-payment_status) | ✓ | `'unpaid'` | Unpaid, partly paid or paid. |
| `notes` | text |  |  | Free-text notes. |
| `attachment_file_id` | uuid |  |  | The supplier's bill as a file, when attached. |
| `posted_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the purchase was posted (numbered, and its stock, ledger and GST entries written). |
| `posted_by` | uuid |  |  | User who posted the purchase. |
| `cancelled_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the purchase was cancelled. A cancelled purchase is kept with its number; cancelling reverses its stock, ledger and GST entries. |
| `cancelled_by` | uuid |  |  | User who cancelled the purchase. |
| `cancel_reason` | text |  |  | Why it was cancelled. |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id. Device the purchase was made on, when it was made offline. |
| `client_id` | uuid |  |  | Id the app gave the purchase when it was made: a retried or offline save with the same id returns the saved purchase instead of making a second one. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |
| `version` | integer | ✓ | `1` | Optimistic locking: increases on every change; a stale write (or an offline edit made on an older copy) is detected by it. |

* Unique `purchases_number_uq`: `(business_id, financial_year, purchase_number)`
* Check `purchases_totals_chk`: `(grand_total >= 0::numeric AND amount_paid >= 0::numeric AND balance_due >= 0::numeric)`
* Index `purchases_client_id_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, client_id) WHERE (client_id IS NOT NULL)`
* Index `purchases_date_idx`: btree `(business_id, received_date)`
* Index `purchases_open_idx`: btree `(business_id, supplier_id) WHERE ((status = 'posted'::document_status) AND (balance_due > (0)::numeric))`
* Index `purchases_supplier_bill_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, supplier_id, supplier_invoice_number, financial_year) WHERE (status <> 'cancelled'::document_status)`
* Index `purchases_supplier_idx`: btree `(business_id, supplier_id, supplier_invoice_date)`
* Trigger `purchases_no_delete_posted`: before delete, each row → `forbid_delete_posted()`
* Trigger `purchases_set_updated_at`: before update, each row → `set_updated_at()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* Referenced by: [`purchase_items`](#purchase_items).purchase_id, [`credit_debit_notes`](#credit_debit_notes).purchase_id, [`payment_allocations`](#payment_allocations).purchase_id

### `purchase_items`

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `purchase_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`purchases`](#purchases).id (on delete cascade). The purchase bill. |
| `line_no` | smallint | ✓ |  | Position of the line on the document (1, 2, 3 ...). |
| `product_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`products`](#products).id. The product sold or bought; its name, HSN and tax are copied onto the line, so later changes to the product do not alter the document. |
| `product_name` | text | ✓ |  | Product name as printed on the document (snapshot). |
| `hsn_code` | varchar(8) |  |  | HSN / SAC code printed on the document (snapshot); GST returns summarise by it. |
| `uqc` | varchar(3) |  |  | GST unit quantity code of the line's unit (NOS, BOX, KGS ...), as reported in the HSN summary. |
| `unit_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`units`](#units).id. The unit the quantity is in (piece, strip, box ...). |
| `conversion_factor` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `1` | Selling/purchase unit -> base unit. |
| `qty` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ |  | Quantity in the line's unit. |
| `free_qty` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `0` | Scheme quantity given free (e.g. 10+1); moves stock, carries no value. |
| `qty_base` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ |  | qty x conversion factor: what the stock ledger moves. |
| `rate` | numeric(15,4) | ✓ |  | Price per unit of the line's unit. |
| `rate_includes_tax` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Whether `rate` already includes GST (tax-inclusive pricing); the taxable value is then worked back from it. |
| `gross_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | qty x rate, before any discount. |
| `discount_percent` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | The line's own discount in percent of the gross amount. |
| `discount_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | The line's own discount in rupees (its percent part plus any flat amount), not counting its share of the document discount. |
| `document_discount_share` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | This line's share of the discount given on the whole document, spread over the lines in proportion to their net amounts. |
| `taxable_value` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | Value GST is charged on: gross less both discounts (taken out of a tax-inclusive rate). |
| `taxability` | [taxability](#enum-taxability) | ✓ | `'taxable'` | Whether the line is taxable, nil-rated, exempt or non-GST (decides the GSTR-1 table it goes to). |
| `tax_category_id` | uuid |  |  | Tax category the rate was resolved from (snapshot; no foreign key). |
| `tax_rate_id` | uuid |  |  | The dated tax rule that applied on the document date (snapshot; no foreign key). |
| `gst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Total GST rate in percent (CGST + SGST, or IGST). |
| `cgst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Central GST rate in percent (intra-state supply). |
| `cgst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Central GST charged on the line. |
| `sgst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | State or Union-territory GST rate in percent (intra-state supply). |
| `sgst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | State or Union-territory GST charged on the line. |
| `igst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Integrated GST rate in percent (inter-state supply, exports and SEZ). |
| `igst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Integrated GST charged on the line. |
| `cess_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Compensation cess rate in percent (tobacco, aerated drinks ...). |
| `cess_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Compensation cess charged on the line (percent part plus any amount per unit). |
| `line_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | Taxable value plus all GST and cess on the line. |
| `batch_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`batches`](#batches).id. The batch the goods came in as (made or found from the batch number). |
| `batch_number` | varchar(40) |  |  | Batch number as printed on the bill. |
| `mfg_date` | date |  |  | Manufacturing date of the batch. |
| `expiry_date` | date |  |  | Expiry date of the batch. |
| `mrp` | numeric(15,4) |  |  | MRP printed on the goods. |
| `landed_unit_cost` | numeric(15,4) | ✓ | `0` | Unit cost per base unit including apportioned freight/charges (landed cost), used for avg cost. |
| `returned_qty` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `0` | Quantity already returned to the supplier (debit notes); no more than the bill quantity can be returned. |

* Check `purchase_items_qty_chk`: `(qty > 0::numeric AND free_qty >= 0::numeric)`
* Index `purchase_items_product_idx`: btree `(business_id, product_id)`
* Index `purchase_items_purchase_idx`: btree `(purchase_id)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `supplier_items`

How a supplier names our products on their bills ("SURF EXL 1KG", item code "HU-1102"). Written when a bill imported from the supplier's file is saved, so the next bill from the same supplier matches line by line on its own. `itemKey` is "c:" + the normalised item code, or "n:" + the normalised name.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `supplier_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`suppliers`](#suppliers).id (on delete cascade). The supplier. |
| `product_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`products`](#products).id (on delete cascade). Our product the supplier's item was matched to. |
| `item_key` | varchar(210) | ✓ |  | The match key: c: + the normalised item code, or n: + the normalised name. |
| `item_code` | varchar(60) |  |  | The supplier's item code, as on their bill. |
| `item_name` | text |  |  | The supplier's item name, as on their bill. |
| `unit_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`units`](#units).id. The unit this supplier bills the item in (a case), when not the stock unit. |
| `last_rate` | numeric(15,4) |  |  | Rate on the supplier's last bill with this item. |
| `last_seen_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the item was last on one of the supplier's bills. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |

* Unique `supplier_items_uq`: `(business_id, supplier_id, item_key)`
* Index `supplier_items_product_idx`: btree `(business_id, product_id)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

| `hsn_code` | varchar(8) |  |  | HSN / SAC code printed on the document (snapshot); GST returns summarise by it. |
| `uqc` | varchar(3) |  |  | GST unit quantity code of the line's unit (NOS, BOX, KGS ...), as reported in the HSN summary. |
| `unit_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`units`](#units).id. The unit the quantity is in (piece, strip, box ...). |
| `conversion_factor` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `1` | Selling/purchase unit -> base unit. |
| `qty` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ |  | Quantity in the line's unit. |

| `qty_base` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ |  | qty x conversion factor: what the stock ledger moves. |
| `rate` | numeric(15,4) | ✓ |  | Price per unit of the line's unit. |
| `rate_includes_tax` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Whether `rate` already includes GST (tax-inclusive pricing); the taxable value is then worked back from it. |
| `gross_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | qty x rate, before any discount. |
| `discount_percent` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | The line's own discount in percent of the gross amount. |
| `discount_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | The line's own discount in rupees (its percent part plus any flat amount), not counting its share of the document discount. |
| `document_discount_share` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | This line's share of the discount given on the whole document, spread over the lines in proportion to their net amounts. |
| `taxable_value` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | Value GST is charged on: gross less both discounts (taken out of a tax-inclusive rate). |
| `taxability` | [taxability](#enum-taxability) | ✓ | `'taxable'` | Whether the line is taxable, nil-rated, exempt or non-GST (decides the GSTR-1 table it goes to). |

| `tax_rate_id` | uuid |  |  | The dated tax rule that applied on the document date (snapshot; no foreign key). |
| `gst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Total GST rate in percent (CGST + SGST, or IGST). |
| `cgst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Central GST rate in percent (intra-state supply). |
| `cgst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Central GST charged on the line. |
| `sgst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | State or Union-territory GST rate in percent (intra-state supply). |
| `sgst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | State or Union-territory GST charged on the line. |

### `invoices`

Tax invoice / bill of supply. Drafts have no number; posting allocates the number, writes stock ledger, party ledger and GST register rows in ONE transaction. Posted invoices are never deleted: they are cancelled (voided), which writes reversing entries and keeps the number.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `invoice_number` | varchar(16) |  |  | GST invoice number (up to 16 letters, digits, / and -), unique in the financial year; empty while a draft. |
| `series_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`document_series`](#document_series).id. Number series the invoice was numbered from. |
| `financial_year` | varchar(9) | ✓ |  | Financial year of the invoice (2026-27); its number is unique within it. |
| `invoice_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date of the invoice (decides the GST period and the tax rules that apply). |
| `due_date` | date |  |  | When payment is due: invoice date + the customer's credit days. |
| `document_kind` | [document_kind](#enum-document_kind) | ✓ | `'tax_invoice'` | Tax invoice, or bill of supply (no GST charged: exempt goods or a composition dealer). |
| `customer_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`customers`](#customers).id. The customer billed. |
| `party_name` | text | ✓ |  | Party's name as printed on the document (snapshot). |
| `party_gstin` | varchar(15) |  |  | Party's GSTIN when the document was posted; empty for unregistered parties. |
| `party_state_code` | char(2) |  |  | Party's GST state code when the document was posted. |
| `billing_address` | jsonb |  |  | Billing address printed on the document (snapshot: line1, line2, city, pincode, state). |
| `shipping_address` | jsonb |  |  | Delivery address printed on the document, when different from billing (snapshot). |
| `place_of_supply` | char(2) | ✓ |  | GST state code of the place of supply (96 for exports): decides CGST + SGST or IGST. |
| `supply_type` | [supply_type](#enum-supply_type) | ✓ |  | Intra-state (CGST + SGST), inter-state (IGST) or export / SEZ. |
| `is_reverse_charge` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Reverse charge: the recipient pays this GST to the government instead of the supplier. |
| `tax_engine_version` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | Version of the calculation engine used (e.g. "gst-line@1"). |
| `sales_order_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`sales_orders`](#sales_orders).id. The order the invoice bills, when it was ordered first. |
| `warehouse_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`warehouses`](#warehouses).id. Godown the goods left from. |
| `price_level_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`price_levels`](#price_levels).id. Price list the invoice was priced on. |
| `salesperson_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`employees`](#employees).id. Salesperson credited with the sale (salesperson-wise reports). |
| `status` | [document_status](#enum-document_status) | ✓ | `'draft'` | Draft, posted or cancelled. |
| `gross_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Sum of the lines' gross amounts (qty x rate). |
| `discount_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | All discounts on the lines, including their shares of the document discount. |
| `document_discount_percent` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Discount on the whole document, in percent of the lines' net total. |
| `document_discount_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Discount on the whole document, in rupees (spread over the lines as `document_discount_share`). |
| `taxable_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total taxable value: the lines' plus taxed charges'. |
| `cgst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total central GST on lines and charges. |
| `sgst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total state / UT GST on lines and charges. |
| `igst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total integrated GST on lines and charges. |
| `cess_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total compensation cess. |
| `charges` | jsonb | ✓ | `'[]'` | Freight, packing etc.: [{key,label,taxable,gstRate,cgst,sgst,igst,cess,total}]. |
| `charges_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Freight, packing and other charges before their GST. |
| `round_off` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Amount added or taken off to round the grand total (to the rupee by default). |
| `grand_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | What the party pays: taxable value + charges + GST and cess + round-off. |
| `amount_paid` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Paid so far against this invoice (payments allocated to it, and payment at the time of the invoice). |
| `balance_due` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Still to be paid: grand total less amount paid and returns / credit notes against it. |
| `payment_status` | [payment_status](#enum-payment_status) | ✓ | `'unpaid'` | Unpaid, partly paid or paid. |
| `cost_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Cost of goods at posting (sum of qty_base x avg cost) for margin reports. |
| `notes` | text |  |  | Free-text notes. |
| `terms` | text |  |  | Terms and conditions printed at the foot of the invoice. |
| `print_locale` | varchar(10) | ✓ | `'en'` | Language the invoice is printed in (can differ from the user's UI language). |
| `irn` | varchar(64) |  |  | Invoice Reference Number from the e-invoice portal (IRP), 64 characters. |
| `irn_ack_number` | varchar(20) |  |  | Acknowledgement number the IRP gave with the IRN. |
| `irn_ack_date` | timestamptz |  |  | Acknowledgement date and time from the IRP. |
| `signed_qr_code` | text |  |  | Signed QR code text from the IRP; the QR code printed on the invoice is drawn from it. |
| `eway_bill_number` | varchar(12) |  |  | E-way bill number (12 digits) for moving the goods. |
| `eway_bill_valid_until` | timestamptz |  |  | Until when the e-way bill is valid. |
| `posted_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the invoice was posted (numbered, and its stock, ledger and GST entries written). |
| `posted_by` | uuid |  |  | User who posted the invoice. |
| `cancelled_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the invoice was cancelled. A cancelled invoice is kept with its number; cancelling reverses its stock, ledger and GST entries. |
| `cancelled_by` | uuid |  |  | User who cancelled the invoice. |
| `cancel_reason` | text |  |  | Why it was cancelled. |
| `revision` | integer | ✓ | `0` | Reserved for editing posted invoices (stays 0: posted invoices are cancelled and made again). |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id. Device the invoice was made on, when it was made offline. |
| `client_id` | uuid |  |  | Idempotency key from the client (offline sync retries cannot create duplicates). |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |
| `version` | integer | ✓ | `1` | Optimistic locking: increases on every change; a stale write (or an offline edit made on an older copy) is detected by it. |
| `zero_rated_type` | varchar(6) |  |  | Zero-rated supply: an export or a supply to an SEZ unit, with or without payment of IGST (EXPWP, EXPWOP, SEZWP, SEZWOP, as GSTR-1 names them); null for other sales. |
| `shipping_bill_number` | varchar(20) |  |  | Exports: the shipping bill and port (often known only after the invoice; can be added later). |
| `shipping_bill_date` | date |  |  | Date of the shipping bill. |
| `port_code` | varchar(6) |  |  | Port code of the shipping bill (6 characters). |
| `lut_arn` | varchar(20) |  |  | Without payment of IGST: the letter of undertaking (ARN) it was made under, printed on the invoice. |
| `eway_bill_date` | timestamptz |  |  | When the e-way bill was generated. |
| `review_status` | [invoice_review_status](#enum-invoice_review_status) |  |  | A bill made offline that broke a rule by the time it reached the server (a price changed meanwhile, the customer or a product was made inactive, its GST month was locked, it was sent over a week late, or stock or credit went past a limit set to block) is accepted, as the customer already has it, and held for a manager: needs_review until someone with invoice.review marks it reviewed. Null for every other bill. |
| `review_reasons` | jsonb |  |  | Why it was held: [{code, params}], codes price_changed, customer_inactive, product_inactive, period_locked, late_sync, stock_short, credit_limit, credit_overdue. |
| `reviewed_by` | uuid |  |  | User who marked it reviewed (or cancelled it while it was held). |
| `reviewed_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When it was marked reviewed. |
| `review_note` | text |  |  | What the reviewer noted (for example the credit note issued for it). |

* Check `invoices_number_format_chk`: `(invoice_number IS NULL OR invoice_number::text ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9/-]{1,16}$'::text)`
* Unique `invoices_number_uq`: `(business_id, financial_year, invoice_number)`
* Check `invoices_posted_number_chk`: `(status = 'draft'::document_status OR invoice_number IS NOT NULL)`
* Check `invoices_totals_chk`: `(grand_total >= 0::numeric AND amount_paid >= 0::numeric AND balance_due >= 0::numeric)`
* Check `invoices_zero_rated_chk`: `(zero_rated_type IS NULL OR (zero_rated_type::text = ANY (ARRAY['EXPWP'::character varying, 'EXPWOP'::character varying, 'SEZWP'::character varying, 'SEZWOP'::character varying]::text[])))`
* Index `invoices_client_id_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, client_id) WHERE (client_id IS NOT NULL)`
* Index `invoices_customer_idx`: btree `(business_id, customer_id, invoice_date)`
* Index `invoices_date_idx`: btree `(business_id, invoice_date)`
* Index `invoices_open_idx`: btree `(business_id, customer_id, due_date) WHERE ((status = 'posted'::document_status) AND (balance_due > (0)::numeric))`
* Index `invoices_review_idx`: btree `(business_id, posted_at) WHERE (review_status = 'needs_review'::invoice_review_status)`
* Index `invoices_salesperson_idx`: btree `(business_id, salesperson_id, invoice_date)`
* Trigger `invoices_no_delete_posted`: before delete, each row → `forbid_delete_posted()`
* Trigger `invoices_period_lock`: before update, each row → `invoices_period_lock_guard()`
* Trigger `invoices_set_updated_at`: before update, each row → `set_updated_at()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* Referenced by: [`invoice_items`](#invoice_items).invoice_id, [`invoice_revisions`](#invoice_revisions).invoice_id, [`dispatch_orders`](#dispatch_orders).invoice_id, [`credit_debit_notes`](#credit_debit_notes).invoice_id, [`payment_allocations`](#payment_allocations).invoice_id, [`suggestion_feedback`](#suggestion_feedback).invoice_id

## Credit and debit notes

### `credit_debit_notes`

Credit and debit notes for both sides:

- customer credit note: sales return / post-sale discount (reduces receivable, outward GST)
- customer debit note: price increase after invoicing
- supplier side: purchase return / supplier credit note (reduces payable, inward GST) When `affects_stock` is true, posting moves stock (sale_return / purchase_return).

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `note_type` | [note_type](#enum-note_type) | ✓ |  | credit (lowers what the party owes, or what we owe a supplier is lowered by their credit) or debit. |
| `party_type` | [party_type](#enum-party_type) | ✓ |  | customer (our note on a sale) or supplier (a note on a purchase). |
| `customer_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`customers`](#customers).id. The customer, for notes on sales. |
| `supplier_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`suppliers`](#suppliers).id. The supplier, for notes on purchases. |
| `note_number` | varchar(16) |  |  | Number from the note series (up to 16 characters, as GST requires), unique per year, type and party side. |
| `party_note_number` | varchar(30) |  |  | Supplier's own note number when we record a note they issued. |
| `series_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`document_series`](#document_series).id. Number series the note was numbered from. |
| `financial_year` | varchar(9) | ✓ |  | Financial year of the note (2026-27); its number is unique within it. |
| `note_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date of the note (decides the GST period). |
| `reason` | [note_reason](#enum-note_reason) | ✓ |  | Sales return, purchase return, discount, rate difference, damage or other. |
| `invoice_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`invoices`](#invoices).id. The invoice the note is against (customer notes). |
| `purchase_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`purchases`](#purchases).id. The purchase bill the note is against (supplier notes). |
| `affects_stock` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Whether goods move: returns bring stock in (or send it back to the supplier); discounts and rate differences move only value. |
| `warehouse_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`warehouses`](#warehouses).id. Godown the returned goods go into or leave from (required when affects_stock). |
| `party_name` | text | ✓ |  | Party's name as printed on the document (snapshot). |
| `party_gstin` | varchar(15) |  |  | Party's GSTIN when the document was posted; empty for unregistered parties. |
| `party_state_code` | char(2) |  |  | Party's GST state code when the document was posted. |
| `billing_address` | jsonb |  |  | Billing address printed on the document (snapshot: line1, line2, city, pincode, state). |
| `shipping_address` | jsonb |  |  | Delivery address printed on the document, when different from billing (snapshot). |
| `place_of_supply` | char(2) | ✓ |  | GST state code of the place of supply (96 for exports): decides CGST + SGST or IGST. |
| `supply_type` | [supply_type](#enum-supply_type) | ✓ |  | Intra-state (CGST + SGST), inter-state (IGST) or export / SEZ. |
| `is_reverse_charge` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Reverse charge: the recipient pays this GST to the government instead of the supplier. |
| `tax_engine_version` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | Version of the calculation engine used (e.g. "gst-line@1"). |
| `status` | [document_status](#enum-document_status) | ✓ | `'draft'` | Draft, posted or cancelled. |
| `gross_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Sum of the lines' gross amounts (qty x rate). |
| `discount_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | All discounts on the lines, including their shares of the document discount. |
| `document_discount_percent` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ | `0` | Discount on the whole document, in percent of the lines' net total. |

| `taxable_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total taxable value: the lines' plus taxed charges'. |
| `cgst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total central GST on lines and charges. |
| `sgst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total state / UT GST on lines and charges. |
| `igst_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total integrated GST on lines and charges. |
| `cess_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Total compensation cess. |
| `charges` | jsonb | ✓ | `'[]'` | Freight, packing etc.: [{key,label,taxable,gstRate,cgst,sgst,igst,cess,total}]. |
| `charges_total` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Freight, packing and other charges before their GST. |
| `round_off` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Amount added or taken off to round the grand total (to the rupee by default). |

| `notes` | text |  |  | Free-text notes. |
| `posted_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the note was posted (numbered, and its stock, ledger and GST entries written). |
| `cancelled_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the note was cancelled. A cancelled note is kept with its number; cancelling reverses its stock, ledger and GST entries. |
| `cancel_reason` | text |  |  | Why it was cancelled. |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id. Device the note was made on, when it was made offline. |
| `client_id` | uuid |  |  | Id the app gave the note when it was made: a retried or offline save with the same id returns the saved note instead of making a second one. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |
| `version` | integer | ✓ | `1` | Optimistic locking: increases on every change; a stale write (or an offline edit made on an older copy) is detected by it. |
| `irn` | varchar(64) |  |  | A credit note to a registered buyer: the e-invoice IRN, acknowledgement and signed QR code from the IRP. |
| `irn_ack_number` | varchar(20) |  |  | Acknowledgement number from the IRP. |
| `irn_ack_date` | timestamptz |  |  | Acknowledgement date and time from the IRP. |
| `signed_qr_code` | text |  |  | Signed QR code text from the IRP, printed as a QR code. |

| `employee_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`employees`](#employees).id. The employee, for salary and advances. |
| `other_party_name` | text |  |  | Name of the party when it is none of the above. |
| `payment_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date the money was received or paid. |
| `amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | Amount of the payment. |
| `method` | [payment_method](#enum-payment_method) | ✓ |  | Cash, UPI, bank transfer, cheque, card or other. |
| `payment_account_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`payment_accounts`](#payment_accounts).id. Account the money went into or came out of. |
| `reference_number` | varchar(40) |  |  | UTR / UPI reference / cheque number / card slip. |
| `cheque_date` | date |  |  | Date written on the cheque. |
| `cheque_bank` | text |  |  | Bank the cheque is drawn on. |
| `cheque_status` | [cheque_status](#enum-cheque_status) |  |  | Pending, deposited, cleared or bounced; a bounced cheque reverses the payment. |
| `unallocated_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Part not yet applied to any bill: an advance or on-account amount, used against later bills. |
| `status` | [document_status](#enum-document_status) | ✓ | `'posted'` | Posted or cancelled. |
| `notes` | text |  |  | Free-text notes. |
| `collected_by_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`employees`](#employees).id. Employee who collected the money (collection reports). |
| `receipt_file_id` | uuid |  |  | Reserved for a photo of the receipt (not filled). |
| `cancelled_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the payment was cancelled (it is kept; its ledger entries are reversed and its allocations released). |
| `cancelled_by` | uuid |  |  | User who cancelled the payment. |
| `cancel_reason` | text |  |  | Why it was cancelled. |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id. Device the payment was made on, when it was made offline. |
| `client_id` | uuid |  |  | Id the app gave the payment when it was made: a retried or offline save with the same id returns the saved payment instead of making a second one. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |
| `version` | integer | ✓ | `1` | Optimistic locking: increases on every change; a stale write (or an offline edit made on an older copy) is detected by it. |

* Check `payments_amount_chk`: `(amount > 0::numeric AND unallocated_amount >= 0::numeric AND unallocated_amount <= amount)`
* Unique `payments_number_uq`: `(business_id, financial_year, direction, payment_number)`
* Check `payments_party_chk`: `(party_type = 'customer'::party_type AND customer_id IS NOT NULL OR party_type = 'supplier'::party_type AND supplier_id IS NOT NULL OR party_type = 'employee'::party_type AND employee_id IS NOT NULL OR party_type = 'other'::party_type)`
* Index `payments_client_id_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, client_id) WHERE (client_id IS NOT NULL)`
* Index `payments_customer_idx`: btree `(business_id, customer_id, payment_date)`
* Index `payments_date_idx`: btree `(business_id, payment_date, method)`
* Index `payments_supplier_idx`: btree `(business_id, supplier_id, payment_date)`
* Trigger `payments_no_delete_posted`: before delete, each row → `forbid_delete_posted()`
* Trigger `payments_set_updated_at`: before update, each row → `set_updated_at()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* Referenced by: [`payment_allocations`](#payment_allocations).payment_id, [`employee_advances`](#employee_advances).payment_id, [`salary_slips`](#salary_slips).payment_id

### `payment_allocations`

Which invoices / bills / notes a payment settles (partial payments, many-to-many).

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `payment_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`payments`](#payments).id. The payment. |
| `invoice_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`invoices`](#invoices).id. The invoice it pays (exactly one of invoice, purchase or note is set). |
| `purchase_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`purchases`](#purchases).id. The purchase bill it pays. |
| `note_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`credit_debit_notes`](#credit_debit_notes).id. The credit or debit note it settles. |
| `amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | Amount applied. |
| `allocated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When it was applied. |
| `allocated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who applied it. |
| `reversed_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the allocation was undone (cancelled payment or bounced cheque). |

* Check `payment_allocations_amount_chk`: `(amount > 0::numeric)`
* Check `payment_allocations_target_chk`: `(num_nonnulls(invoice_id, purchase_id, note_id) = 1)`
* Index `payment_allocations_invoice_idx`: btree `(invoice_id)`
* Index `payment_allocations_payment_idx`: btree `(payment_id)`
* Index `payment_allocations_purchase_idx`: btree `(purchase_id)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `party_ledger_entries`

PARTY LEDGER — customer and supplier account statements. Append-only like the stock ledger. Customer: invoice = debit, payment/credit note = credit. Supplier: purchase = credit, payment/debit note = debit.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | ✓ | identity (always) | **Primary key.** Sequential row number (append-only table). |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `party_type` | [party_type](#enum-party_type) | ✓ |  | customer or supplier. |
| `customer_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`customers`](#customers).id. The customer, for customer entries. |
| `supplier_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`suppliers`](#suppliers).id. The supplier, for supplier entries. |
| `entry_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date of the entry (the document's date). |
| `doc_type` | varchar(30) | ✓ |  | Source document: invoice, payment, credit_note, purchase, opening ... |
| `doc_id` | uuid |  |  | Id of the source document. |
| `doc_number` | varchar(40) |  |  | Number of the source document, for statements. |
| `debit` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Debit amount: what a customer owes more (or what we owe a supplier less). |
| `credit` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Credit amount: what a customer owes less (or what we owe a supplier more). |
| `narration` | text |  |  | Line shown on the statement. |
| `reverses_entry_id` | bigint |  |  | Set on entries that reverse an earlier one (cancellations). |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |

* Check `party_ledger_amount_chk`: `(debit >= 0::numeric AND credit >= 0::numeric AND (debit > 0::numeric) <> (credit > 0::numeric))`
* Check `party_ledger_party_chk`: `(party_type = 'customer'::party_type AND customer_id IS NOT NULL AND supplier_id IS NULL OR party_type = 'supplier'::party_type AND supplier_id IS NOT NULL AND customer_id IS NULL)`
* Index `party_ledger_customer_idx`: btree `(business_id, customer_id, entry_date, id)`
* Index `party_ledger_doc_idx`: btree `(doc_type, doc_id)`
* Index `party_ledger_supplier_idx`: btree `(business_id, supplier_id, entry_date, id)`
* Trigger `party_ledger_entries_append_only`: before delete or update, each row → `forbid_update_delete()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* **The API's role may:** read, insert (not update or delete).

### `collection_notes`

A collector's visit when the money did not come: a note ("shop closed") or the customer's promise to pay by a date (and how much, if they said). Shown on Outstanding; a promise stays open until the customer next pays.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `customer_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`customers`](#customers).id. The customer visited. |
| `kind` | varchar(10) | ✓ |  | promise \| note |
| `note` | text |  |  | Free-text note. |
| `promised_amount` | numeric(15,2) |  |  | How much the customer said they would pay, if they said. |
| `promised_on` | date |  |  | Date the customer promised to pay by (required for a promise). |
| `visited_on` | date | ✓ |  | Date of the visit. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |

* Check `collection_notes_kind_chk`: `(kind::text = ANY (ARRAY['promise'::character varying, 'note'::character varying]::text[]))`
* Check `collection_notes_promise_chk`: `(kind::text <> 'promise'::text OR promised_on IS NOT NULL)`
* Index `collection_notes_customer_idx`: btree `(business_id, customer_id, created_at)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

## GST returns and configuration

### `gst_transactions`

GST REGISTER — one row per taxable line of every posted GST document, written in the same transaction that posts the document. It stores FACTS (who, where, what, how much tax), not return classifications: whether a row lands in B2CL or B2CS, which table of GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B, is decided by the versioned return formatter for the period, using thresholds from configuration. A rule change therefore never requires rewriting history.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | ✓ | identity (always) | **Primary key.** Sequential row number (append-only table). |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `direction` | [gst_direction](#enum-gst_direction) | ✓ |  | outward (sales: GSTR-1, GSTR-3B 3.1) or inward (purchases and expenses: input credit). |
| `doc_type` | [gst_doc_type](#enum-gst_doc_type) | ✓ |  | invoice, credit_note, debit_note, purchase, purchase_credit_note, purchase_debit_note or expense. |
| `doc_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | Id of the source document. |
| `doc_line_id` | uuid |  |  | Id of the source document's line. |
| `doc_number` | varchar(30) | ✓ |  | Number of the document as it goes into the return. |
| `doc_date` | date | ✓ |  | Date of the document. |
| `original_doc_number` | varchar(30) |  |  | Original invoice for credit/debit notes. |
| `original_doc_date` | date |  |  | Date of that original invoice. |
| `return_period` | char(7) | ✓ |  | "YYYY-MM" return period the row belongs to. |
| `party_name` | text |  |  | Party's name on the document. |
| `party_gstin` | varchar(15) |  |  | Party's GSTIN (empty for unregistered parties): B2B rows have one. |
| `party_registration` | [party_gst_registration](#enum-party_gst_registration) | ✓ |  | Party's GST status (regular, composition, consumer, SEZ, overseas ...). |
| `party_state_code` | char(2) |  |  | Party's state. |
| `place_of_supply` | char(2) | ✓ |  | Place of supply (GST state code; 96 for exports). |
| `supply_type` | [supply_type](#enum-supply_type) | ✓ |  | Intra-state, inter-state or export / SEZ. |
| `is_reverse_charge` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Tax payable by the recipient under reverse charge (GSTR-3B 3.1(d) for purchases). |
| `taxability` | [taxability](#enum-taxability) | ✓ |  | Taxable, nil-rated, exempt or non-GST. |
| `hsn_code` | varchar(8) |  |  | HSN / SAC code, for the HSN summary. |
| `uqc` | varchar(3) |  |  | Unit quantity code, for the HSN summary. |
| `qty` | numeric(15,3) | ✓ | `0` | Quantity in that unit, for the HSN summary. |
| `taxable_value` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | Taxable value of the line. |
| `gst_rate` | numeric(7,3) | ✓ |  | GST rate in percent. |
| `cgst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Central GST. |
| `sgst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | State / UT GST. |
| `igst_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Integrated GST. |
| `cess_amount` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ | `0` | Compensation cess. |
| `document_value` | numeric(15,2) | ✓ |  | Whole-document value (needed for B2CL threshold tests and invoice-level return tables). |
| `itc_eligibility` | [itc_eligibility](#enum-itc_eligibility) |  |  | For inward rows: whether the credit can be claimed (GSTR-3B table 4). |
| `is_cancelled` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Set when the source document is cancelled; formatters exclude or report as cancelled. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `zero_rated_type` | varchar(6) |  |  | Export / supply to SEZ (EXPWP, EXPWOP, SEZWP, SEZWOP): reported in their own GSTR-1 tables and GSTR-3B 3.1(b). |

* Check `gst_transactions_period_chk`: `(return_period ~ '^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]\|1[0-2])$'::text)`
* Index `gst_transactions_doc_idx`: btree `(doc_type, doc_id)`
* Index `gst_transactions_hsn_idx`: btree `(business_id, return_period, hsn_code)`
* Index `gst_transactions_period_idx`: btree `(business_id, return_period, direction, doc_type)`
* Trigger `gst_transactions_guard`: before delete or update, each row → `gst_transactions_guard()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* **The API's role may:** read, insert, update (not delete).

### `gst_return_periods`

Return periods. Locking a period (after filing GSTR-1) blocks edits and cancellations of documents dated in it; corrections then go through credit/debit notes in an open period.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `return_type` | varchar(12) | ✓ |  | GSTR1 or GSTR3B. |
| `period` | char(7) | ✓ |  | Return period, YYYY-MM. |
| `status` | [gst_period_status](#enum-gst_period_status) | ✓ | `'open'` | open, locked (documents dated in it can no longer change their tax) or filed. |
| `locked_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the period was locked. |
| `locked_by` | uuid |  |  | User who locked it. |
| `filed_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the filing was recorded. |
| `arn` | varchar(30) |  |  | Acknowledgement reference number of the filed return. |
| `notes` | text |  |  | Free-text notes. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |

* Unique `gst_return_periods_uq`: `(business_id, return_type, period)`
* Trigger `gst_return_periods_set_updated_at`: before update, each row → `set_updated_at()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
