## System: audit log, notifications, outbox, sync, backups

### `audit_logs`

AUDIT LOG — append-only (trigger + revoked privileges). Written by the API's service layer inside the same transaction as the change it describes. `changes` = {"field": [old, new]} for updates; full snapshot for creates/deletes. Partition by month (created_at) once it grows past tens of millions of rows.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | ✓ | identity (always) | **Primary key.** Sequential row number (append-only table). |
| `business_id` | uuid |  |  | The business the action was in (empty for sign-in events before a business is chosen). |
| `user_id` | uuid |  |  | Who did it. |
| `user_name` | text |  |  | Their name at the time (kept even if the user is renamed). |
| `action` | varchar(60) | ✓ |  | e.g. invoice.updated, invoice.cancelled, stock.adjusted, role.permissions_changed, login.failed |
| `entity_type` | varchar(40) |  |  | Kind of record changed (invoice, customer, role ...). |
| `entity_id` | uuid |  |  | Id of the record changed. |
| `entity_label` | text |  |  | Human label, e.g. "INV/26-27/10023". |
| `changes` | jsonb |  |  | What changed: {"field": [old, new]} for edits, the whole record for creates and deletes. |
| `ip` | varchar(45) |  |  | IP address of the request. |
| `user_agent` | text |  |  | Browser or app of the request. |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | Registered device, when known. |
| `request_id` | varchar(40) |  |  | Id of the API request (matches the server log). |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |

* Index `audit_logs_entity_idx`: btree `(business_id, entity_type, entity_id, created_at)`
* Index `audit_logs_time_idx`: btree `(business_id, created_at)`
* Index `audit_logs_user_idx`: btree `(business_id, user_id, created_at)`
* Trigger `audit_logs_append_only`: before delete or update, each row → `forbid_update_delete()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation` (all commands), using `((business_id = (NULLIF(current_setting('app.business_id'::text, true), ''::text))::uuid) OR ((business_id IS NULL) AND (user_id = (NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id'::text, true), ''::text))::uuid)))`
* **The API's role may:** read, insert (not update or delete).

### `notifications`

In-app notifications. Stored as a translation key + params (never rendered text), so each user sees them in their own language.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `user_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`users`](#users).id. null = everyone with `permission`. |
| `permission` | varchar(60) |  |  | Shown to everyone whose role has this permission (when user_id is empty). |
| `type` | varchar(40) | ✓ |  | What it is about (payment_due, low_stock ...). |
| `severity` | [notification_severity](#enum-notification_severity) | ✓ | `'info'` | info, success, warning or critical. |
| `title_key` | varchar(80) | ✓ |  | Translation key of the title (each person sees it in their own language). |
| `body_key` | varchar(80) |  |  | Translation key of the text. |
| `params` | jsonb | ✓ | `'{}'` | Values put into the title and text (names, amounts, dates), as JSON. |
| `entity_type` | varchar(40) |  |  | Kind of record it is about, to open it. |
| `entity_id` | uuid |  |  | Id of that record. |
| `dedupe_key` | varchar(120) |  |  | Makes "once per condition" a database rule: a reminder for the same thing (e.g. "low_stock:2026-09-24", "order:&lt;id>:packed") is never created twice. |
| `delivered_channels` | varchar(20)[] |  |  | Channels it went out on: in_app, and push once FCM accepted it for at least one phone. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |

* Index `notifications_business_created_idx`: btree `(business_id, created_at)`
* Index `notifications_dedupe_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, dedupe_key) WHERE (dedupe_key IS NOT NULL)`
* Index `notifications_user_idx`: btree `(user_id, created_at) WHERE (user_id IS NOT NULL)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)
* Referenced by: [`notification_receipts`](#notification_receipts).notification_id

### `notification_receipts`

Each person's state of a notification: read, or dismissed (hidden from their list). A notification addressed to everyone with a permission is read by each of them separately. No row: not read yet.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `notification_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `user_id`). → [`notifications`](#notifications).id (on delete cascade). The notification. |
| `user_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `notification_id`). → [`users`](#users).id. The person. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `read_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When they read it (opened it, or marked all read). |
| `dismissed_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When they dismissed it. |

* Primary key `notification_id, user_id`
* Index `notification_receipts_user_idx`: btree `(user_id, business_id)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `push_tokens`

Phones that get notifications as push messages through Firebase Cloud Messaging (the Android app): one row per business and app install, for the person signed in on it, who gets what they may see in the inbox. The app registers its token at each start and removes it when signing out; a token FCM says is no longer valid is deleted.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `user_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`users`](#users).id (on delete cascade). The person signed in on the phone. |
| `device_id` | uuid |  |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id (on delete set null). The phone's registered device (offline work), when it has one. |
| `session_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | The sign-in it was registered in (refresh_tokens.family_id): pushes stop when it ends or moves to another business. |
| `token` | text | ✓ |  | The registration token the app got from Firebase (secret to the phone: whoever has it can send to it through the project). |
| `platform` | varchar(10) | ✓ |  | android (ios later). |
| `locale` | varchar(5) | ✓ | `'en'` | The app's language when it registered: pushes are written in it. |
| `last_seen_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the app last registered it (it does at each start). |
| `last_push_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When FCM last accepted a push for it. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |

* Index `push_tokens_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, token)`
* Index `push_tokens_user_idx`: btree `(business_id, user_id)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `reminder_rules`

Which reminders run and how, one row per business and type (the types and their defaults are REMINDERS in @digitalbahi/core). `config` holds the hour of the daily check and the type's own settings.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |

| `config` | jsonb | ✓ | `'{}'` | The rule's settings as JSON (days before due, thresholds, time of day ...). |

| `is_active` | boolean | ✓ | `true` | Switched off: no daily check and no event notifications of this type. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `last_run_on` | date |  |  | The business day its daily check last ran (claimed): once a day, even with several API servers. |
| `last_run_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When an hourly rule's check last ran (claimed): once an hour; what changed since is what it looks at. |

* Trigger `reminder_rules_set_updated_at`: before update, each row → `set_updated_at()`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `outbox_events`

Transactional outbox: domain events written in the business transaction and processed asynchronously (purchase-history stats, report summaries, search index, notifications, webhooks). Guarantees nothing is lost if a worker is down.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | bigint | ✓ | identity (always) | **Primary key.** Sequential row number (append-only table). |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | The business the event happened in. |
| `event_type` | varchar(60) | ✓ |  | What happened: invoice.posted, invoice.cancelled, payment.received, credit_note.posted, purchase.posted ... |
| `aggregate_type` | varchar(40) | ✓ |  | Kind of record (invoice, payment ...). |
| `aggregate_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | Id of the record. |
| `payload` | jsonb | ✓ |  | Details the handlers need, as JSON. |
| `attempts` | smallint | ✓ | `0` | Times a handler tried and failed. |
| `last_error` | text |  |  | The last failure, for the error log. |
| `available_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | Not handed to a worker before this time (retries wait longer each time). |
| `processed_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When it was handled; empty while waiting. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |

* Index `outbox_events_business_pending_idx`: btree `(business_id, id) WHERE (processed_at IS NULL)`
* Index `outbox_events_pending_idx`: btree `(available_at) WHERE (processed_at IS NULL)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `sync_mutations`

Server-side log of mutations received from offline devices. The client's mutation id is the primary key, so replaying the same queue twice is a no-op (idempotent sync). Kept for the planned /sync/push protocol: offline work is sent today through the ordinary endpoints with an Idempotency-Key, and this table is not written.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `device_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`devices`](#devices).id. Device that sent it. |
| `user_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | Person who made it. |
| `mutation_type` | varchar(40) | ✓ |  | Kind of change (invoice.create, payment.create ...). |
| `entity_id` | uuid |  |  | Record the change is about. |
| `base_version` | integer |  |  | Version of the record the device had (for conflict detection). |
| `payload_hash` | varchar(64) | ✓ |  | SHA-256 of what was sent, to tell a replay from a different change. |
| `status` | [sync_mutation_status](#enum-sync_mutation_status) | ✓ |  | applied, rejected or conflict. |
| `result` | jsonb |  |  | What the server answered, returned again on a replay. |
| `client_created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ |  | When the change was made on the device. |
| `received_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the server received it. |

* Index `sync_mutations_device_idx`: btree `(device_id, received_at)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `sync_changes`

The pull feed's change log (Phase 5.3): which products, customers and suppliers changed, by transaction. Triggers on those tables (and on prices, barcodes, units and stock balances, for their product) add a row per record per transaction; nothing updates a row, so concurrent bills never wait on it. A device asks for everything from transactions at or after the oldest one still running when it last asked (GET /sync/pull), so a change that commits late is never missed. Rows older than 30 days are deleted nightly; a device that last pulled before that reloads the whole business.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `xid`, `entity`, `entity_id`). → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `entity` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `business_id`, `xid`, `entity_id`). What changed: product, customer or supplier. |
| `entity_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `business_id`, `xid`, `entity`). The record (for a price, barcode, unit or stock balance: its product). |
| `xid` | xid8 | ✓ | `pg_current_xact_id()` | **Primary key** (with `business_id`, `entity`, `entity_id`). The transaction that changed it. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When, for deleting old rows. |

* Primary key `business_id, xid, entity, entity_id`
* Index `sync_changes_created_idx`: btree `(created_at)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

| `size_bytes` | bigint |  |  | Size of the backup file. |

### `backup_schedules`

Automatic backups: a password-protected copy emailed on a schedule, one row per business. The password is encrypted with the API's field cipher and never returned. `next_run_at` is when the scheduler next sends a copy.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Unique.** → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `frequency` | varchar(10) | ✓ | `'off'` | off \| daily \| weekly |
| `weekday` | smallint | ✓ | `0` | 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday (weekly only). |
| `hour` | smallint | ✓ | `21` | Hour of the day in the business's time zone. |
| `email_to` | text |  |  | Empty: the business's own email. |
| `passphrase` | text |  |  | Password the copies are protected with, encrypted; never shown again. |
| `next_run_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the next copy goes out. |
| `last_run_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When the last copy was tried. |
| `last_status` | varchar(10) |  |  | sent or failed. |
| `last_error` | text |  |  | Why the last copy failed (e.g. the mail server refused it). |
| `configured_by` | uuid |  |  | Whose name the automatic backups go out under (the person who set it up). |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |

* Index `backup_schedules_due_idx`: btree `(next_run_at)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `report_views`

SAVED REPORT VIEWS — a report's tab and settings (period, grouping, filters) kept under a name to open again. Private to the person who saved it unless shared with the team; others see a shared view only for a report their role opens. A period like "this month" is kept as that, not as dates.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `user_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`users`](#users).id. Person who saved the view. |
| `name` | varchar(60) | ✓ |  | Name of the view (unique per person, ignoring case). |
| `report` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | insights \| sales \| collections \| purchases \| outstanding \| profit \| pnl \| products |
| `settings` | jsonb | ✓ | `'{}'` | The report's tab, period, grouping and filters, as JSON. |
| `shared` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Shown to the team (to roles that may open the report), not only to its owner. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |

* Index `report_views_name_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, user_id, lower((name)::text))`
* Index `report_views_shared_idx`: btree `(business_id, shared)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

## Analytics (derived, rebuildable)

### `customer_product_stats`

Per customer x product purchase history: powers invoice suggestions (see docs/07).

| `customer_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `product_id`). → [`customers`](#customers).id (on delete cascade). The customer. |
| `product_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `customer_id`). → [`products`](#products).id (on delete cascade). The product. |
| `order_count` | integer | ✓ |  | Invoices in the window that had the product (several lines on one invoice count once). |

### `product_associations`

Store-wide "frequently bought together" rules (A -> B).

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |

| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `product_id`, `related_product_id`). → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |

| `related_product_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Primary key** (with `business_id`, `product_id`). → [`products`](#products).id (on delete cascade). Product B (suggested with it). |
| `pair_count` | integer | ✓ |  | Bills in the window with both A and B. |

### `analytics_runs`

Runs of the nightly analytics job, one per business and day. Inserting the row claims the run, so two API servers never both do it. `details` keeps what it found: customers rebuilt, drift between the worker's figures and a fresh computation, association rules mined, and cached balances that do not match their ledgers.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `job` | varchar(30) | ✓ |  | Which job: nightly. |
| `as_of` | date | ✓ |  | The business day the run is for. |
| `status` | varchar(12) | ✓ | `'running'` | running, completed or failed. |
| `started_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the run was claimed and began. |
| `finished_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When it completed or failed. |
| `details` | jsonb | ✓ | `'{}'` | What the run found, as JSON (counts, drift, mismatched balances with examples). |
| `error` | text |  |  | Why it failed. |

* Check `analytics_runs_status_chk`: `(status::text = ANY (ARRAY['running'::character varying, 'completed'::character varying, 'failed'::character varying]::text[]))`
* Unique `analytics_runs_uq`: `(business_id, job, as_of)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

## WhatsApp and email

### `messaging_settings`

How a business sends WhatsApp and email: its own WhatsApp Business number (Meta Cloud API, or a provider's webhook) and the platform's mail server or its own SMTP. Secrets (access token, webhook secret, SMTP password) are encrypted with the API's field cipher and never returned.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | **Unique.** → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `whatsapp_provider` | varchar(20) | ✓ | `'none'` | none \| meta \| webhook |
| `whatsapp_number` | varchar(20) |  |  | The business's WhatsApp number as customers see it. |
| `whatsapp_phone_number_id` | varchar(40) |  |  | Meta Cloud API phone number id of the business's WhatsApp number. |
| `whatsapp_webhook_url` | text |  |  | The provider's address messages are posted to (webhook provider). |
| `whatsapp_secret` | text |  |  | Meta access token or the webhook's signing secret (encrypted). |
| `whatsapp_document_template` | varchar(100) |  |  | Approved templates: a bill with a document header, and a payment reminder. |
| `whatsapp_reminder_template` | varchar(100) |  |  | Name of the approved template for payment reminders. |
| `whatsapp_template_language` | varchar(10) | ✓ | `'en'` | Language code of the templates (en, hi ...). |
| `email_mode` | varchar(20) | ✓ | `'platform'` | none \| platform \| smtp |
| `smtp_host` | text |  |  | The firm's own mail server (smtp mode). |
| `smtp_port` | integer |  |  | Its port (465 with SSL, 587 with STARTTLS). |
| `smtp_secure` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Connect with SSL/TLS from the start (port 465). |
| `smtp_user` | text |  |  | User name on the mail server. |
| `smtp_password` | text |  |  | Password on the mail server, encrypted; never returned. |
| `email_from_name` | varchar(100) |  |  | Name the emails come from (the firm's name by default). |
| `email_from_address` | text |  |  | Address the emails come from. |

| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |
| `whatsapp_status_key` | varchar(40) |  |  | **Unique.** Delivery ticks: the random key in the address Meta (or the provider) calls back with "delivered" / "read", also Meta's verify token. |
| `whatsapp_app_secret` | text |  |  | Meta app secret that signs those callbacks (encrypted). |
| `whatsapp_template_language_hi` | varchar(10) |  |  | Language code of the same templates approved in Hindi (hi), for customers who get messages in Hindi; null: they get the default language's. |
| `sms_provider` | varchar(20) | ✓ | `'none'` | none \| webhook: the business's SMS gateway, which receives signed JSON {to, text, senderId, templateId}. |
| `sms_webhook_url` | text |  |  | The gateway's address. |
| `sms_secret` | text |  |  | The secret the requests are signed with (encrypted). |
| `sms_sender_id` | varchar(10) |  |  | DLT sender id (header) the SMS come from, e.g. DGBAHI. |
| `sms_reminder_template` | varchar(40) |  |  | DLT template id registered for the payment reminder in English. |
| `sms_reminder_template_hi` | varchar(40) |  |  | DLT template id registered for the payment reminder in Hindi. |

* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

### `messages`

Every WhatsApp and email sent (or tried) to a customer or supplier.

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|:-:|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | ✓ | `gen_random_uuid()` | **Primary key.** UUIDv7 made by the application (time-ordered, creatable on an offline device); the default is a safety net. |
| `business_id` | uuid | ✓ |  | → [`businesses`](#businesses).id (on delete restrict). The business (tenant) the row belongs to. Row-level security shows a connection only the rows of its current business. |
| `channel` | [message_channel](#enum-message_channel) | ✓ |  | whatsapp, email or sms. |
| `kind` | varchar(20) | ✓ |  | invoice \| note \| receipt \| reminder \| backup \| test |
| `document_id` | uuid |  |  | The invoice, note or receipt sent. |
| `document_number` | varchar(40) |  |  | Its number, for the log. |
| `party_type` | [party_type](#enum-party_type) |  |  | customer or supplier. |
| `party_id` | uuid |  |  | The customer or supplier. |
| `party_name` | text |  |  | Their name at the time. |
| `recipient` | text | ✓ |  | WhatsApp or SMS number (international digits) or email address it went to. |
| `subject` | text |  |  | Email subject. |
| `body` | text | ✓ |  | The text sent. |
| `attachment_name` | text |  |  | File name of the PDF attached. |
| `template` | jsonb |  |  | The WhatsApp template and its parameters, when one was used. |
| `locale` | varchar(10) | ✓ | `'en'` | Language of the message (en or hi). |
| `status` | [message_status](#enum-message_status) | ✓ | `'queued'` | queued, sent, delivered, read or failed. |
| `provider` | varchar(20) |  |  | Who sent it: meta, webhook or smtp; log in test mode (recorded, not sent). |
| `provider_message_id` | text |  |  | The provider's id for the message, matched by the status callbacks. |
| `error` | text |  |  | Why sending failed. |
| `attempts` | integer | ✓ | `0` | Times sending was tried. |
| `sent_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When it was sent. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was created. |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | ✓ | `now()` | When the row was last changed; kept by the `set_updated_at` trigger. |
| `created_by` | uuid |  |  | User who created the row (informational: users are deactivated, never deleted, so there is no foreign key). |
| `updated_by` | uuid |  |  | User who last changed the row (informational, no foreign key). |
| `delivered_at` | timestamptz |  |  | WhatsApp ticks, from the provider's status callbacks. |
| `read_at` | timestamptz |  |  | When WhatsApp reported it read. |
| `automatic` | boolean | ✓ | `false` | Sent by a rule (automatic payment reminders), not by a person. |
| `reminder_on` | date |  |  | The business day an automatic reminder went for: the rule's schedule counts these (one per customer and day). |

* Index `messages_auto_reminder_uq`: unique, btree `(business_id, party_id, reminder_on) WHERE automatic`
* Index `messages_business_created_idx`: btree `(business_id, created_at)`
* Index `messages_document_idx`: btree `(business_id, document_id)`
* Index `messages_queued_idx`: btree `(business_id, status)`
* Row-level security: policy `tenant_isolation`, rows of the current business only (`app.business_id`)

## Functions

Written in the migrations; triggers use them to keep the rules no application bug can break.

| Function | Returns | Language | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device_check(p_id uuid, p_hash text)` | text | plpgsql | A device checking in with its secret, signed in or not: removed devices are told to delete their copy. Row-level security hides every device without a business chosen, so this answers only "active / removed" for the one device whose secret matches (anything else is "unknown"). |
| `due_backup_schedules(p_now timestamp with time zone, p_limit integer)` | TABLE(business_id uuid, user_id uuid) | sql | The businesses whose automatic backup is due, for the API's scheduler. It runs without a session, and row-level security hides every business's schedule until one is chosen; this answers only "whose turn is it" (the schedule itself is then claimed and read inside that business). |
| `forbid_delete_posted()` | trigger | plpgsql | Posted financial documents are cancelled (voided), never physically deleted. Trigger on [`stock_adjustments`](#stock_adjustments), [`purchases`](#purchases), [`invoices`](#invoices), [`credit_debit_notes`](#credit_debit_notes), [`payments`](#payments), [`expenses`](#expenses). |
| `forbid_update_delete()` | trigger | plpgsql | Ledgers and the audit log are append-only. Corrections are new rows. Trigger on [`stock_ledger`](#stock_ledger), [`party_ledger_entries`](#party_ledger_entries), [`audit_logs`](#audit_logs). |
| `gst_period_locked(p_business uuid, p_date date)` | boolean | sql | GST period lock: once GSTR-1 for a month is locked/filed, invoices and notes dated in it cannot change their tax-relevant content or be cancelled. Payment fields (amount_paid, balance_due, payment_status) stay updatable. |
| `gst_transactions_guard()` | trigger | plpgsql | GST register rows may only be flagged as cancelled, never edited or deleted. Trigger on [`gst_transactions`](#gst_transactions). |
| `invoices_period_lock_guard()` | trigger | plpgsql | Trigger on [`invoices`](#invoices). |
| `nightly_analytics_due(p_now timestamp with time zone, p_hour integer, p_limit integer)` | TABLE(business_id uuid, time_zone text) | sql | The businesses due for the nightly analytics run: active ones where it is past p_hour in their own time zone and no run is claimed for their current date yet. Without a session, row-level security hides businesses and runs; this answers only "whose turn is it" (the run is claimed and done inside that business). |
| `outbox_pending_businesses(p_now timestamp with time zone, p_limit integer)` | TABLE(business_id uuid) | sql | The businesses with outbox events waiting, for the API's outbox worker. It runs without a session, and row-level security hides every business's events until one is chosen; this answers only "whose events are waiting" (the events are then taken and handled inside that business). |
| `reminder_rules_due(p_now timestamp with time zone, p_limit integer)` | TABLE(business_id uuid, time_zone text) | sql | The businesses with a reminder check due: an active rule whose hour (config.hour, else 10 for leave_request, salary_due and customer_reminders, 9 for the rest) has come in the business's time zone and that has not run since: hourly rules (orders_waiting, REMINDERS[...].hourly in @digitalbahi/core) an hour after their last run (last_run_at), the others once per business day (last_run_on). Without a session, row-level security hides businesses and rules; this answers only "whose turn is it" (the rules are then claimed and checked inside that business). |
| `set_updated_at()` | trigger | plpgsql | updated_at is maintained automatically on every table that has it. Trigger on 55 tables. |
| `track_sync_change()` | trigger | plpgsql | Records that a product, customer or supplier changed in this transaction (once per record per transaction). TG_ARGV[0] is the entity, TG_ARGV[1] the column holding its id. SECURITY DEFINER: a change made in any context (a restore, a job) is recorded, whatever the session's business. Trigger on [`customers`](#customers), [`suppliers`](#suppliers), [`products`](#products), [`product_units`](#product_units), [`product_barcodes`](#product_barcodes), [`product_prices`](#product_prices), [`stock_balances`](#stock_balances). |
| `user_in_other_business(p_user uuid, p_business uuid)` | boolean | sql | Whether a member's account is also in another business. A business may set the user ID and password only of accounts it alone uses (its staff), never of someone who also works elsewhere. Row-level security hides other businesses' memberships from the API, so this answers the one question with the owner's rights and nothing more. |
| `whatsapp_status_business(p_key text)` | uuid | sql | The business a status callback belongs to, from the key in its address. Callbacks come without a session, and row-level security hides every business's settings until one is chosen; this answers only that question. |
